It does not cover the 2023 target year. Biography is a sympathetic academic profile; author-editor position is not declared."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","5B.7","5B.8"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The phrase 'highest share for any Mexican presidential candidate in recent history' is not supported by the excerpt. The excerpt confirms the election date (1 July 2018), the vote percentage (53.2% rounded, consistent with 53.19%), the opponents (Anaya and Meade), and the victory context. The claim about the platform emphasis on austerity, anti-corruption, and social welfare is substantiated by other locators (blocks 5, 65) but not by block 1 directly. El Gobierno municipal se resistió a implementar el Seguro Popular, aprobado por el Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS) y basado en la aportaciones de cuotas por los beneficiarios, aduciendo que los defeños ya recibían de sus instituciones municipales la necesaria cobertura social y además gratuita.","locator":"extracted HTML block 21","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"DF government (2000-2005) predates the 2023 target year; provides governance philosophy evidence. Program name, refusal to implement Seguro Popular, and the exact reasoning ('los defeños ya recibían de sus instituciones municipales la necesaria cobertura social y además gratuita') are all confirmed verbatim. Minor formatting note: 'apoyaciones' in draft should be 'aportaciones' per source text."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0003","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"In March 2004, Televisa broadcast clandestine videos ('videoescándalo') showing López Obrador's close collaborators — Gustavo Ponce Meléndez (DF Finance Secretary), René Bejarano (his former chief of staff and PRD legislative coordinator), and Carlos Ímaz (Tlalpan delegation head) — gambling thousands of dollars at Las Vegas casinos and negotiating/collecting cash payments from businessman Carlos Ahumada Kurtz. All three were charged with fraud and money laundering. Rosario Robles (PRD president 2002-2003) was forced to leave the party. López Obrador's response was delayed and tepid, framing the scandal as a 'conspiracy' by ex-president Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, and the Fox administration.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Gustavo Ponce Meléndez, René Bejarano, Carlos Ímaz, Carlos Ahumada Kurtz, Rosario Robles, López Obrador","action":"caught receiving cash payments from businessman and gambling in Las Vegas casinos; López Obrador characterized exposure as political conspiracy","mechanism":"Televisa broadcast of clandestine videos; criminal charges for fraud and money laundering","outcome":"Three collaborators charged; Robles forced out of PRD; López Obrador framed scandal as political persecution rather than acknowledging corruption among his inner circle","dates":["March 2004"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"En marzo de 2004, en un momento que a muchos no les pareció casual, estalló el llamado videoescándalo, la emisión por la cadena Televisa de unas grabaciones de vídeo clandestinas que mostraban a prominentes políticos y funcionarios, la mayoría miembros del PRD y colaboradores estrechos de López Obrador, en situaciones altamente comprometedoras... Los tres habían sido grabados mientras se dedicaban a actividades lúdicas como jugarse a la ruleta miles de dólares en un lujoso casino de Las Vegas y a otras mucho más alarmantes, como negociar con Ahumada la compra de favores políticos o recoger de sus manos ingentes sumas de dinero.","locator":"extracted HTML block 22","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"March 2004 predates the 2023 target year but is directly relevant to evaluating whether López Obradar would enforce anti-corruption rules against his own political associates — a question applicable to his 2023 presidency.","source_limitations":["March 2004 predates 2023 by 19 years. This is the most directly relevant evidence in the source for 5B.5 conduct, but it concerns DF government associates, not federal-level conduct in 2023."],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The core events (Televisa broadcast, names of collaborators, gambling in Las Vegas, negotiating/collecting cash from Ahumada) are fully confirmed by the excerpt. However: (1) The excerpt does not name the three individuals specifically; it says 'prominentes políticos y funcionarios, la mayoría miembros del PRD y colaboradores estrechos de López Obrador' and later 'Los tres habían sido grabados' — the names (Ponce Meléndez, Bejarano, Ímaz) are provided in locator 23, not block 22 directly. (2) The excerpt does not state the charges were specifically 'fraud and money laundering' — it says Ahumada 'se apresuró a presentar contra los implicados una denuncia por extorsión' and later mentions criminal charges but the specific罪名 are not in block 22. (3) The conspiracy framing (Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, Fox) is not in block 22; it appears in block 23. Draft should be corrected to note these elements come from block 23, not block 22. The core gambling and cash negotiation facts are verified."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0004","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"The 2018 campaign platform of the Juntos Haremos Historia coalition (MORENA, PT, PES) pledged 'austeridad republicana' — reorienting public resources from operating costs to investment without raising taxes, plus 100 billion pesos in first-year savings. The program included social programs targeting poverty and vulnerable groups, increased domestic gasoline production to reduce imports, energy and food self-sufficiency, anti-corruption pledges, and defense of Mexican migrants against Trump's border policies.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"López Obrador and Juntos Haremos Historia coalition","action":"promulgated 2018 campaign platform with austerity, social spending, energy self-sufficiency, and anti-corruption commitments","mechanism":"published Project 2018 / Project Alternative of Nation 2018-2024; campaign literature","outcome":"Platform formed the basis for the December 2018 inauguration and subsequent policy direction","dates":["2018 campaign period","December 2018 inauguration"],"quantities":["100,000 million pesos savings in first year promised"],"excerpt":"El programa electoral incidía en una serie de temas: la 'austeridad republicana', para reorientar los recursos públicos de los gastos corrientes a la inversión sin subir los impuestos; la atención de las 'causas sociales', combatiendo la pobreza y elevando el desarrollo humano de los colectivos vulnerables, de una violencia criminal desmedida y cuyas escalofriantes cifras son las propias de un país en guerra civil; el principio de la retirada de las Fuerzas Armadas de las misiones de seguridad interna pero sin precipitaciones, con la meta de 'pacificar' México en tres años; el aumento de la oferta de gasolina autóctona para reducir las importaciones y rebajar precios; las autosuficiencias energética y alimentaria, en el caso del agro ofreciendo a los productores locales precios de garantía; la 'erradicación' de la corrupción política 'dando ejemplo' desde Los Pinos; y la defensa firme de los migrantes mexicanos, más en tiempos de muro fronterizo de Trump y de renegociación forzada del TLCAN, buscando con Estados Unidos unas relaciones de cooperación y buena vecindad basadas 'en el respeto mutuo'.","locator":"extracted HTML block 5","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"The source was published November 2018 and documents only the announced platform and early transition actions, not the executed budget outcomes of 2023. There is a 4+ year gap between the announced program and the target year.","source_limitations":["Campaign platform announced in 2018 — a promise, not an executed record. No evidence of actual 2023 budget composition or execution is available from this source. The biography cannot evaluate implementation."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The excerpt confirms 'austeridad republicana' with resource reorientation without tax increases, social programs for poverty and vulnerable groups, increased domestic gasoline production, energy and food self-sufficiency, anti-corruption ('erradicación de la corrupción política dando ejemplo'), and defense of migrants against Trump's wall and TLCAN renegotiation. However: (1) The 100 billion pesos figure appears in block 31, not block 5. The draft attributes this quantity to block 5's excerpt. (2) The phrase 'sin subir los impuestos' in block 5 is consistent with 'without raising taxes' but the draft's phrasing implies a quantified first-year savings target of 100 billion pesos, which is not in block 5. Corrected to note 100 billion peso savings comes from block 31, not block 5. Otherwise the core platform elements are verified."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0005","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"López Obrador publicly pledged that anti-corruption enforcement under his presidency would include no persecution or vengeance: 'We declare emphatically that what is needed is justice, not revenge, we hate no one' and 'I am not going to put Peña Nieto in jail.' Truth Commissions would investigate FOBAPROA and PEMEX without criminal prosecution of individuals.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador (as president-elect and candidate)","action":"pledged justice without vengeance, no persecution, and Truth Commissions rather than prosecutions for former presidents","mechanism":"campaign speeches; victory speech; IV Congress presentation November 2017","outcome":"Promise of limited accountability for prior administrations; explicit commitment against prosecutorial pursuit of ex-presidents","dates":["November 2017 (IV Congress)","16 March 2018 (INE registration)","July 2018 (victory speech)"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"'Declaramos enfáticamente que lo que se necesita es justicia, no venganza, no odiamos a nadie', subrayó el candidato... 'No voy a meter a Peña Nieto en la cárcel', aseguró también durante la campaña... las investigaciones para el esclarecimiento de los abusos incluirían el caso del FOBAPROA y a Pemex, objetos de escrutinio por sendas comisiones de la verdad aunque, eso sí, no habría 'persecución contra nadie'.","locator":"extracted HTML block 60","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"November 2017 campaign period; does not cover 2023 actual anti-corruption enforcement record. Cannot evaluate whether this pledge was kept or violated in 2023.","source_limitations":["Campaign-period pledge, not an observed governance outcome. However: (1) The quote attribution is to 'el candidato' in the context of the IV Congress (November 2017), not necessarily 'victory speech' or 'INE registration.' The draft lists three date contexts (November 2017, March 2018, July 2018) but block 60 only covers the IV Congress November 2017 event. The other dates may be accurate but are not confirmed by block 60's excerpt. (2) The phrase 'Truth Commissions would investigate FOBAPROA and PEMEX without criminal prosecution of individuals' is partially supported — the excerpt says 'FOBAPROA y Pemex, objetos de escrutinio por sendas comisiones de la verdad aunque, eso sí, no habría persecución contra nadie' — confirming commissions of truth and no persecution, but the excerpt does not explicitly state 'without criminal prosecution of individuals.' This is a reasonable inference but not a direct quote. Accept with minor correction to remove the date inference."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0006","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"In his July 2018 victory speech, López Obrador pledged: 'No mentir, no robar, no traicionar al pueblo' (not to lie, not to steal, not to betray the people); promised corruption eradication regardless of position ('incluye a compañeros de lucha, funcionarios, amigos y familiares'); and declared 'por el bien de todos, primero los pobres' (for the good of all, the poor first). The coalition won supermajorities in both federal chambers: 308/500 deputies and 69/128 senators.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"López Obrador","action":"made explicit anti-corruption and pro-poor priority pledges in victory speech; MORENA coalition secured legislative supermajority","mechanism":"victory speech at Zócalo; July 2018 election results","outcome":"Legislative supermajority enabling passage of MORENA agenda; explicit corruption eradication pledge with universal application","dates":["2 July 2018 (victory speech)","July 2018 (congressional elections)"],"quantities":["308/500 deputies","69/128 senators","53.19% of presidential vote"],"excerpt":"'Bajo ninguna circunstancia, el próximo presidente permitirá la corrupción ni la impunidad. Sobre aviso no hay engaño: sea quien sea, será castigado. Incluyo a compañeros de lucha, funcionarios, amigos y familiares'... 'Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres'... en la Cámara de Diputados, los tres partidos de Juntos Haremos Historia sumaban 308 escaños de 500 y en el Senado 69 escaños de 128.","locator":"extracted HTML block 65","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"July 2018 election and victory speech; provides stated governance priorities and mandate scope. Biography published November 2018 does not cover 2023 execution of these pledges."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","5B.7","5B.8"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The excerpt partially confirms the draft. Block 65 contains the corruption and impunity quote ('Bajo ninguna circunstancia, el próximo presidente permitirá la corrupción ni la impunidad. Sobre aviso no hay engaño...') and the 'Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres' quote, and the legislative numbers. The specific 'no mentir, no robar, no traicionar al pueblo' triada appears in block 65 of unit-0065 (the same locator), but the excerpt provided in block 65 (unit-0065) does not contain the exact 'no mentir, no robar' formulation. The corruption eradication pledge regardless of position is confirmed. The 'Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres' is confirmed. The legislative numbers 308/500 and 69/128 are confirmed. The 53.19% vote figure is also in block 65 but the specific excerpt provided does not contain it — it is in the same locator. Accept with correction: the 'no mentir, no robar, no traicionar' triada is not in the provided excerpt, though it is in the same locator block."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0007","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"The 2018 campaign platform characterized López Obrador's governance philosophy as 'pragmatic social democracy' accepting free market principles, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, peso floatation, and Bank of Mexico autonomy, combined with rejection of neoliberalism, privatization, and foreign takeover of strategic sectors, prioritizing national production and domestic consumption. He promised to create the National Guard, pursue Santa Lucía Airport (not NAIM), provide free internet nationwide, implement gender equality in labor, and run the Becas Estudiantiles 'Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro' youth employment program.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador and MORENA coalition","action":"articulated hybrid economic philosophy combining market orthodoxy with nationalist protectionism and announced specific infrastructure and social program commitments","mechanism":"Project Alternative of Nation 2018-2024; campaign presentations","outcome":"Framework for 2018-2024 presidency combining macroeconomic discipline with state-directed development and social welfare","dates":["November 2017 (IV Congress)","2018 campaign"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Su plataforma para el período de gobierno 2018-2024 sugiere una socialdemocracia pragmática que asume las nociones orthodoxas del libre mercado, la estabilidad macroeconómica, la disciplina presupuestaria y la flotación del peso, conjugadas, eso sí, con el rechazo a las 'tendencias privatizadoras' y la 'extranjerización' de sectores estratégicos, y la prioridad para la 'producción nacional'.","locator":"extracted HTML block 6","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"Campaign-period policy framework announcement (November 2017 to 2018). Does not cover 2023 actual policy execution or outcomes. The biography was published November 2018.","source_limitations":["Announced policy framework, not observed 2023 governance outcomes. No evidence of actual macroeconomic management, regulatory enforcement, or budget execution in 2023 is available from this source."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The economic philosophy description ('pragmatic social democracy,' free market principles, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, peso floatation, rejection of privatization and foreign takeover, national production priority) is fully confirmed by the excerpt. However, the draft adds several specific policy commitments (National Guard, Santa Lucía Airport, free internet, gender equality in labor, Becas Estudiantiles 'Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro') that are NOT in block 6's excerpt. These appear in block 64, not block 6. The draft mixes content from two different locators (blocks 6 and 64) and attributes everything to block 6. Additionally, Bank of Mexico autonomy is not in block 6's excerpt. Accept with correction: the specific infrastructure and social program commitments come from block 64, not block 6. The economic philosophy section is verified against block 6."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0008","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"López Obrador lost the July 2006 presidential election to Felipe Calderón by 0.58% (243,934 votes) — 35.89% to 35.31%. The EU observer mission and international community recognized Calderón's victory. These are historical behavioral patterns, not 2023 governance evidence. The source does not cover whether this pattern persisted into the 2023 presidency."],"question_ids":["5B.7","5B.5"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The core claim about self-proclamation as 'presidente legítimo,' alternate government, and rejection of the result is confirmed by the excerpt. However: (1) The margin figures (0.58%, 243,934 votes, 35.89% vs 35.31%) are NOT in block 3's excerpt. The excerpt says 'por los pelos' (narrowly) and '0,56%' in unit-0003, not 0.58%. The exact figures 35.89% vs 35.31% are not in the provided excerpt. (2) The EU observer mission recognition is not in block 3's excerpt — unit-0003 mentions 'la comunidad internacional' broadly but not the EU mission specifically; EU mission appears in block 33. (3) The 2012 repetition is mentioned in block 3 (second paragraph) — 'En 2012, al cabo de seis años...' — but the claim about the pattern of rejection being 'repeated' in 2012 is supported by block 3. Accept with correction: the specific vote percentages and margins come from block 33, not block 3; EU mission specifically from block 33."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0009","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"During the 2018 USMCA trade renegotiation and migration crisis, López Obrador's administration offered work visas to Central American migrants while Trump threatened to 'permanently' close the US border in November 2018, which would have caused enormous commercial damage to Mexico. El 26 de noviembre, tras un intento de asalto repelido con gases lacrimógenos por la Policía estadounidense, Trump —cuya hija Ivanka va a asistir a la toma de protesta o posesión junto con elvicepresidente Mike Pence — amenazó con cerrar la frontera 'permanentemente', lo que de suceder acarrearía enormes daños comerciales a México.","locator":"extracted HTML block 7","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"2018 late transition/early administration period; provides evidence on external shock management approach. Does not cover 2023 shock response directly.","source_limitations":["2018 transition period; 4+ years before 2023. No evidence of actual 2023 shock management (inflation, debt, commodity shocks) available from this source."],"question_ids":["5B.9"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The core elements are confirmed: USMCA negotiations, López Obrador considering it beneficial, migration caravans through Mexico, Trump's 'permanent' border closure threat on November 26, and the commercial damage language. The excerpt says 'López Obrador, anticipándose al clima de rechazo extendido en la ciudadanía, habló de solidaridad y de ofrecer visas de trabajo a estos migrantes' — this anecdote is actually in block 7 but not in the provided excerpt for block 7.
